title: Reduction of the flat model
statement:
Let $A_{E,m}$ and $A_{E,n}$ be two finite coefficient stages with
$m\leq n$, let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, let
$K\in D^b_c(T,A_{E,n})$ be a bounded constructible complex of
$A_{E,n}$-modules on the small pro-étale site or on the small étale
site, and let $P\cong K$ be a bounded flat model of $K$ in degrees
$[a,b]$ in the sense of [lem-sf-flat-model]: each $P^q$ is a flat
$A_{E,n}$-module sheaf and $P^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. Write
$K_m=K\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ for the reduction of $K$. Then
$P\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ is a bounded flat model of $K_m$ in the
same interval:

$$
K_m\cong P\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m},\qquad
(P\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m})^q=0\quad(q\notin[a,b]),
$$

and each term $P^q\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ is a flat
$A_{E,m}$-module sheaf. Consequently the reduction $K_m$ has finite
Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ as soon
as $K$ does.

proof.text: Work on either of the two sites, and put $R=(A_{E,n})_T$ and $S=(A_{E,m})_T$. The quotient homomorphism $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ is induced by the identity of $\mathcal O_E$, since $\varpi_E^n=\varpi_E^m\varpi_E^{n-m}$ gives $(\varpi_E^n)\subseteq(\varpi_E^m)$ for $m\le n$; it induces the coefficient-ring-sheaf morphism $\varphi:R\to S$. Choose the site skeleton and module values in the ambient coefficient universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. The site is therefore essentially small in that universe, as required by the K-flatness lemma; the finite coefficient rings are viewed in the same universe. The given $P$ is bounded above by $b$ and has flat terms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] on this ringed site to conclude that $P$ is K-flat. This is the precise bounded-above-flat result needed in the first sentence of the blueprint proof; no assertion about arbitrary unbounded double complexes is used.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; blueprint proof, first sentence

proof.text: Let $Q_R,Q_S$ denote passage from complexes to the corresponding derived categories. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], derived extension of scalars along $\varphi$ is computed by ordinary termwise change of rings on the K-flat complex $P$. Apply the derived functor to the given isomorphism $K\cong Q_R(P)$, and compute its value at $P$ (using the identity K-flat resolution of $P$). This gives, in $D(S)$, $K_m\cong Q_S(P\otimes_R S)$. Thus the reduction retains its $S$-module structure; we do not identify an object of $D(S)$ with its restriction to $D(R)$. This proves the displayed derived-category isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, for the identity morphism of topoi with coefficient map R to S

proof.text: Set $P_m=P\otimes_R S$ with termwise differentials $d_P^q\otimes1$. Apply [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] to the same $\varphi$ and $P$: the K-flatness proved in step 1 and the assumed flatness of every $P^q$ give that $P_m$ is K-flat over $S$ and every $P_m^q=P^q\otimes_R S$ is a flat $S$-module sheaf. The support assertion is elementary from the sheafified sectionwise tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]: if $q\notin[a,b]$, then $P^q=0$, so the presheaf with sections $P^q(U)\otimes_{R(U)}S(U)$ is zero and its sheafification is zero. Therefore $P_m^q=0$ outside $[a,b]$. Together with step 2 this is exactly the required bounded flat model.

For any sheaf $M$ of $S$-modules placed in degree zero, use the K-flat representative $P_m$ of step 3 in the derived-tensor construction: [def-weil-derived-tensor] on the pro-etale site, or [def-kun-derived-tensor] on the etale site. It computes $K_m\otimes_S^L M$ as $Q_S(P_m\otimes_S M[0])$. By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] the degree-$q$ term is $P_m^q\otimes_S M$, because the only nonzero degree of $M[0]$ is zero. This term vanishes when $q\notin[a,b]$. In such a degree its cohomology is zero: its kernel is a subobject of the zero degree-$q$ term and the quotient by the incoming image is therefore zero, by [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. This is the defining test for Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] or [def-kun-tor-amplitude], respectively. It establishes the last assertion, in fact from the supplied bounded flat model alone.
